11.t: Working with data: force on a ramp
q: What force was needed at 30 cm?
Higher ramp, more force: roughly a straight line.
Calculate the ideal force at 30 cm and compare.
10 × 0.3 / 1 = 3.0 N; measured 3.5 N is 0.5 N more.
Explain why the line does not pass through zero.
Even on a flat ramp a force is needed to overcome friction, about 0.4 N here.
